title: Search for the best stock plan

blocks.text: The substation team now wants the stocking plan itself. Some spares *must* be stocked (a regulator requires them); the rest compete for what is left of the budget. `bound` and `by_ratio` are written for you in `search.py`; you write the search.
The model, with $`S`$ the spares, $`M \subseteq S`$ the must-stock ones and $`D = S \setminus M`$:

Write `best_plan(items, budget, must)`. `items` is a list of `(name, value, cost)` with whole values and costs above 0, and `must` a set of names. Return `(value, names)`: the best plan's total value, must-stock items included, and the sorted list of every stocked name. Return `None` when the must-stock items alone cost more than the budget.

Use the given pieces as lesson 3.2.4's search does: sort the free items once with `by_ratio`, keep a stack of fixings (dicts from name to 0 or 1, starting with `{}`), and at each node call `bound(order, budget_left, fixed)`, which returns `None` for an infeasible node or `(value, split, taken)`. Prune infeasible nodes, prune a node when $`\lfloor \text{value} \rfloor`$ is not above the incumbent, take `taken` as the new plan when `split` is `None`, and otherwise push the children `split = 0` and `split = 1`.

cases.says: five spares: budgets of 50 and 100 give plans worth 220 and 310
on 20 random 12-item instances, one per seed, the value matches brute force
items that must be stocked appear in the plan and their values count in its total
when the items that must be stocked cost more than the budget, the answer is None

origin.section: Check the Search Against Brute Force and Against HiGHS

concepts: a search is checked against brute force and an independent solver on many instances
items fixed at 1 are paid first, items fixed at 0 are skipped, and the free items keep their order
the budget-only selection: must-dos paid first, one 0-1 variable per other project, one budget row
the search pops fixings from a stack, prunes three ways, and pushes both children of the split item
